description: issue #775 (review gate, QA finding B3): `wait -1.5` -- a count that is BOTH non-whole AND out of range, the only input class that can observe the order of the two checks. `spec/interaction-events.md`'s `### wait <n>` orders them explicitly ("a non-whole count raises `ol-type`, and a negative count raises `ol-range`"), the same TYPE-before-RANGE ordering `spec/commands.md`'s `repeat` entry states ("The checks are ordered: if `count` is not a whole number it raises `ol-type` ...; otherwise, if it is negative, it raises `ol-range`"). Every other count fixture in the corpus is non-whole OR out of range, never both, so an implementation that ran the range check FIRST would pass the entire corpus while reporting `ol-range` here. That mutation survived a fully green run until this fixture existed. Getting the order wrong is not cosmetic: it would put a FRACTIONAL value into an `ol-range` count diagnostic, which `spec/error-model.md`'s `ol-range` entry scopes to a negative WHOLE-number count while `:99` makes a wrong-typed value `ol-type` -- and it would silently split `wait`/`every` from `repeat`, which is the cross-form consistency this whole change exists to establish. Its `every` twin is `every/every-negative-non-whole`. As with every other failed `wait` validation the `primitive` event is NOT emitted, only the instruction event precedes the diagnostic, and the span covers just the argument.

diagnostics.message: wait needs a whole number, but got a number.
